items.analysis: The SRS contains captured software requirements for the mission computer, but it lacks requirements for COTS, GOTS, MOTS, OSS, or reused software components. Furthermore, approval status is marked as 'Draft for Review' and maintenance processes cannot be verified from the document alone.
items.rationale: Software requirements are established and recorded within the SRS document. However, requirements for COTS, GOTS, MOTS, OSS, or reused software components are completely absent, and formal approval/maintenance records reside outside the document.

evidence.excerpt: This Software Requirements Specification defines the software requirements for the Starhawk Space Fighter Mission Computer (SFMC).

external_evidence_needed: Software Development Plan (SDP)
Software Configuration Management Plan
Change Control Board (CCB) approval records and signature sheets
COTS/GOTS/MOTS/OSS trade studies and software reuse evaluation records

items.analysis: The SRS lists high-level mission needs and contains derived requirements across operational modes and subsystems. However, the requirement traceability matrix is explicitly identified as incomplete, multiple requirements remain unresolved open items, and requirements analysis activities cannot be proven solely by the specification.
items.rationale: High-level mission needs are mapped in Section 10, but the document explicitly states that a complete requirement-to-mission-need traceability matrix has not yet been developed and leaves key parameters unresolved in Section 11.

evidence.excerpt: A complete requirement-to-mission-need traceability matrix has not yet been developed.

external_evidence_needed: Top-level Systems Engineering Requirements Specification
System and Software Safety Analysis Reports (e.g., Hazard Analysis)
Hardware Interface Control Documents (ICDs) and Specifications
Software Requirements Analysis and Trade Study reports

items.analysis: The SRS includes specific safety constraints, controls, mitigations, and operational assumptions across hardware, operator, and software interfaces, such as friendly-fire prevention, emergency priorities, and mandatory pilot override.
items.rationale: Software-related safety constraints and controls are explicitly documented in the SRS, including restrictions on firing at friendly spacecraft, automated threat countermeasures, and pilot command override capabilities.

evidence.excerpt: The SFMC shall never permit the pilot to fire a weapon at a friendly spacecraft.
The pilot shall always be able to override automatic spacecraft controls.

external_evidence_needed: System Hazard Analysis (SHA) and System Safety Plan
Software System Safety Technical Report
Hazard Tracking System logs showing hazard mitigation mapping to SRS requirements

items.analysis: Tracking and managing requirement changes is an ongoing project management and configuration management process. A single static draft SRS document cannot show whether changes are actively tracked or managed.
items.rationale: The requirement mandates a management process for tracking and managing changes over time, which cannot be assessed from the contents of the SRS itself.
external_evidence_needed: Software Configuration Management Plan
Change Control Board (CCB) meeting minutes
Software Change Requests (SCRs) and Change Request tracking repository
Version control repository commit logs and baseline history

items.analysis: Identifying, initiating corrective actions, and tracking inconsistencies to closure is an active project management quality process. While the SRS identifies open items in Section 11, the execution of the tracking and closure process cannot be assessed from the document.
items.rationale: Tracking inconsistencies among requirements, plans, and products to closure is a management process. The SRS lists unresolved items but cannot demonstrate process closure.

evidence.excerpt: The following items remain to be resolved during development:

external_evidence_needed: Corrective Action Tracking System / Discrepancy Reports
Software Quality Assurance (SQA) audit reports and inconsistency logs
Requirements Verification Matrix
CCB action item logs and closure records

items.analysis: Performing requirements validation to ensure software performs as intended in the customer environment is an operational/testing process with stakeholders that cannot be established from the SRS text alone.
items.rationale: Requirements validation is a project process involving customer reviews, simulations, or operational evaluations that cannot be proven by the static text of an SRS.
external_evidence_needed: Software Validation Plan
Requirements Validation Review (RVR) reports and stakeholder sign-offs
Operational Concept Document (OpsCon) validation feedback
User-in-the-loop simulation and prototype test reports
